title: Invariant-projection counterexamples for every irrational rotation

issues.description: The remark says the result contradicts Cho-Ko-Lee Corollary 2.8 at mu=1. This depends on the exact hypotheses of the cited corollary, which I could not check against the source. It is a side claim and is not used in the main proof.
issues.evidence: Corollary~\ref{cor:transitive-commutant} contradicts the hyperinvariant-subspace assertion of \citet[Corollary~2.8, p.~801]{cho-ko-lee} at $\mu=1$

coverage: I read sections 00-05 (introduction, parameters, fields, couplings, obstruction, continuity) in full and checked each step. Lemma 1.1 (scalar sampling): I checked the kernel mass, the L2 and second-moment bounds, the Fejer-kernel rectangle estimate and the size of the Fourier error. Prop 1.3: I checked the spread union bound (exponent 4/5-(19/20)^2<0), the lower-range bound a<=|k|lambda<=1/2, the greedy power separation, and the second-moment computation for Z versus Z^id (the equal-power term P^{-1}(8h^{-1}log m)^m goes to 0, and ||Z^id-1||^2 goes to 0 because mh^2=m^{-1/5}). I also checked the realization by characters. For the fields section I checked the fiber representation, the covariance of p, the ergodicity argument in Lemma positive-diagonal, the Lusin and Portmanteau steps in compact-transfer, the sign of the crossing criterion, the positive-orbit identity through (SD)^n=S^n diag F_n(sigma^k x), and the trimming estimates in rational-graphs (a q_a l_j<=(j+1)^{-2}, future mass 4Q_j/K_{j+1}). Couplings: raw density <=10, L2 bound 40kappa^2/m+10/m, product-density lemma, y^(D) ordering and rationality, and the conditional label posteriors including 1/r*<w/2. Obstruction: P(E_j)>=e^{-90} (numerically (m-1)log(1-61/m)~-72.4 at m=200), the D_j bounds on the coefficients, the masked-tail Cauchy-Schwarz with conditional bounds, coverage of all |k|>K_j by the tag, a_s and b_s ranges, crossing intensity m_s rho_s>=L_j, and the final parameter inequality. Continuity: the smoothing, relocation and background coboundary identities (I re-derived the signs), divergence of the integral, the direction of H_b T_f = e^{-1} T_* H_b and the affiliated-transport trace argument, and quasinilpotence. I only skimmed the appendix.
main_claim: For every irrational theta there is a continuous f:T->[0,1] with exactly one zero (at 1) and integral of log f equal to -infinity such that U f(V) has no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite II_1 factor R_theta. This answers the Zhu-Fang-Shi question negatively. The operator is nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent.
